results.problem: Maximum Weighted Clique Enumeration (via Maximum Weighted Independent Set on the complement graph)
results.bound: $440 \to 281$ vertices and $1868 \to 1076$ conflict edges ($36.1\%$ fewer logical variables, $42.4\%$ fewer conflict edges) on an 819-sample SARS-CoV-2 instance
results.quote: Thus, relative to the original residual graph, the combined deterministic reductions remove 36.1% of the logical variables and 42.4% of the conflict edges.

results.bound: $\lambda / w_{\max} = 0.1$ maximizes the proportion of low-energy subgraphs that repair to MWCs on small enumerable graphs
results.previous_best: Lagrange multiplier at least as large as the largest vertex weight (e.g., twice the largest)
results.quote: Taking small graph examples for which we can enumerate all possible subgraphs, and by applying the postprocessing methodology above to the low-energy subgraphs, we see that taking the ratio between the Lagrange multiplier and the highest vertex weight to be 0.1 gives the highest proportion of subgraphs that yield MWCs.

results.bound: modified QAOA recovers more distinct certified MWCs than random-shot baseline in each of ten runs of 20,000 shots on a 64-vertex graph
results.quote: On a graph with 64 vertices, the modified QAOA procedure recovered more distinct certified MWCs than the random shot baseline in each of the ten reported runs.

Our solver-agnostic approach has the potential to completely reduce the input graph: in one instance, the residual graph could be completed exactly after a reduction from 64 to five edge-free vertices.
